title: What If Earth's Core Stopped Keeping Up With the Planet?

scenes.text: What if Earth's inner core stopped keeping up with the planet? Some scientists say it already has.
It's a solid ball of iron and nickel, more than three thousand miles under your feet.
A 2023 study of repeating earthquakes found it began slowing around 2010. It now spins slightly slower than the mantle.
The study suggests a seventy-year cycle, with the last turning point in the early 1970s.
The effect on a day? Maybe a thousandth of a second. You would never notice.
Other scientists think the cycle is only twenty to thirty years. Nobody has seen the core. We only listen to it.

description:
What if Earth's inner core stopped keeping up with the planet?
A 2023 study says it began slowing around 2010, which may change a day by about a thousandth of a second. Other scientists dispute the cycle.
